title: Tutor agreement
heading: Who this is between
body:
This agreement is between @family. ("the platform") and you, as an independent self-employed tutor. It sets out how work is offered, how you are paid, and what each of us is responsible for.

It is not a contract of employment and does not make you an employee or a worker of @family.

title: Tutor agreement
heading: Your status
body:
You are in business on your own account. You are free to tutor for other agencies, for families directly, and for anyone else, including in Merton and Wandsworth. Nothing here is exclusive.

- You are not entitled to holiday pay, sick pay, pension contributions or notice
- You are not subject to appraisal, discipline or line management by the platform
- You decide how you teach: your methods, your pace, your explanations

title: Tutor agreement
heading: Your rate
body:
**You set your own rate.** You tell the platform what you charge for a one-to-one session and you can change it by giving reasonable notice, which for sessions already booked means from the end of the current term.

Where a session has more than one student, your rate increases by a fixed fraction for each additional student, applied to your base rate. That fraction is shown on your profile and does not change without your agreement.

The platform's fee is deducted from what the family pays, and the split in force is shown on your profile. If the platform ever wants to change that split it will ask you, and you can decline.

title: Tutor agreement
heading: How work is offered
body:
Each piece of work is offered separately. The platform will tell you the student, the subject, the venue, the times and the rate, and you either accept it or you don't.

The platform is under no obligation to offer you work, and you are under no obligation to accept any work offered. Declining does not affect what you are offered afterwards. There are no minimum hours and no guaranteed sessions.

Accepting an offer creates a commitment for that work only. It does not commit either of us to anything beyond it.

title: Tutor agreement
heading: Sending someone else
body: You may send a suitably qualified substitute to deliver a session you have accepted, provided they hold a current enhanced DBS certificate and you tell the platform before the session. You remain responsible for paying them and for the quality of the session.

title: Tutor agreement
heading: Tax and National Insurance
body:
You are responsible for your own income tax and National Insurance, and for registering with HMRC as self-employed. The platform does not operate PAYE on your payments and makes no deductions for tax.

If HMRC or anyone else later decides tax should have been deducted, you are responsible for it.

If you trade through a company or partnership, tell the platform so payments are made correctly.

title: Tutor agreement
heading: Payment
body:
Sessions are invoiced to the platform at the end of each month, or generated for you from the sessions recorded in the app if you would rather. Payment is made within 14 days of the invoice.

You are responsible for keeping your session records accurate.

If a family cancels a session with less than 24 hours' notice, they are charged in full and you are paid in full. If a student simply does not turn up, the same applies.

title: Tutor agreement
heading: Insurance and checks
body:
Before your first session you must hold, and keep current:

- An enhanced DBS certificate covering work with children
- Public liability insurance of at least £1,000,000
- Professional indemnity insurance of at least £1,000,000

Send the platform a copy of each on request. This is a condition of taking work through the platform and is not a matter of the platform controlling how you work.

Some families or partner organisations require higher cover. Where they do, you will be told before you accept the work.

title: Tutor agreement
heading: Safeguarding
body:
Everyone tutoring through @family. must follow the platform's safeguarding policy, which is published separately and may be updated.

The core of it is short: sessions happen in the arranged venue or online with the family's knowledge; you do not contact a student privately outside the arranged channels; you report any concern about a child's welfare to the platform the same day, and to the local authority if it is urgent.

Nothing in this agreement prevents you from reporting a safeguarding concern to anyone.

title: Tutor agreement
heading: Where you teach
body:
Sessions take place at the venue agreed when the work was offered — a family's home, a hired room, or online.

Before your first session at a new venue, satisfy yourself that it is safe and suitable for the student and for you, and tell the platform if it is not. If something changes that makes a venue unsafe or unsuitable, tell the platform straight away and do not carry on there.

Do not teach a student at your own home, and do not take a student anywhere that was not agreed.

title: Tutor agreement
heading: Cancellation
body: If you cannot deliver a session you have accepted, tell the platform as soon as you know, and no later than 24 hours before where that is possible. Repeated late cancellation may mean fewer offers of work, which is a commercial decision rather than a disciplinary one.

title: Tutor agreement
heading: Your materials
body:
Anything you write or make yourself stays yours. Material the platform supplies stays the platform's and is for use with @family. students.

If you upload something to the platform, you are giving it permission to use that material with its students, and you keep the right to use it anywhere else.

title: Tutor agreement
heading: Confidentiality
body:
You will keep student and family information confidential and use it only for teaching them. Do not share it with anyone outside the platform without the family's consent.

This continues after you stop taking work through the platform. It does not stop you using your own skills, experience and general knowledge anywhere you like.

title: Tutor agreement
heading: Handling personal information
body:
You will often hold personal information about students — names, contact details, school reports, and sometimes health, SEND or safeguarding information. That last kind is special category data and the law treats it seriously.

You must:

- keep it only as long as you need it for teaching that student, and no longer than six years
- keep it somewhere secure, not in a shared or unlocked device
- not send it to anyone outside the platform without the family's consent, unless the law requires it
- tell the platform the same day if you lose a device or anything might have been exposed
- return or delete it when you stop working with that student, if the platform asks

Both of us must comply with UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018.

title: Tutor agreement
heading: Records and reporting
body:
Keep a record of each session: whether the student attended, what you covered, and how they got on. Record it in the app where you can.

Tell the platform the same day if a student misses a session, and let the platform know early if attendance, progress or behaviour is giving you concern.

title: Tutor agreement
heading: Not going round the platform
body: For six months after your last session with a family introduced to you by @family., please do not take that family on directly outside the platform. Families you already knew, or who found you independently, are yours and always were — just tell the platform if that applies so there is no confusion later.

title: Tutor agreement
heading: Ending it
body:
Either of us can end this arrangement at any time, in writing, with no notice required. Sessions already booked should be honoured or handed over.

If you are handing a student over, write a short note for whoever picks them up: what you covered, where the student is strong, and what still needs work.

title: Tutor agreement
heading: Changes
body:
If these terms change, a new version appears here and you will be asked to read and agree to it. The version you agreed to and the date are recorded. Until you agree to a new version, the one you agreed to is the one that applies.

This agreement is governed by the law of England and Wales.
